metric.why: A facility can have enough total cooling and still starve individual racks; airflow and pressure sensors find recirculation, bypass, and leaks that temperature averages hide.
metric.definition: Cubic feet per minute delivered through the room or containment system, and the pressure differential that drives it through equipment rather than around it.

reading.body:
Airflow and static pressure measurement reveals cooling failures that temperature readings alone cannot detect, making it essential for operating data centers at the density required by AI workloads.

A facility's total cooling capacity is meaningless if air recirculates around equipment instead of flowing through it. Airflow volume in cubic feet per minute and the pressure differential driving that flow expose bypass routes, leaks, and dead zones where hot exhaust mixes back into intake. Temperature sensors average these problems away. At the rack density AI demands, undetected recirculation can cause localized hotspots that trigger throttling or failures even while the room's mean temperature appears acceptable.

This metric matters because power delivery and cooling delivery are now coupled constraints. More compute per square foot requires more precise air distribution. Pressure differential directly indicates whether the system design is working as intended or whether money spent on cooling capacity is being wasted through poor containment and routing.

The metric does not capture the full thermal picture alone. Airflow and pressure must be read alongside temperature, humidity, and liquid coolant data to diagnose whether a cooling problem stems from insufficient capacity, poor design, or operational drift.
